description: HTML structure contracts for the identity transform. Documents the BEM selectors, data attributes, and HTML structure the engine produces for each rune. Auto-generated from theme config — do not edit by hand.

tint.description: Per-rune colour override (SPEC-053): a named tint from the theme registry, with inline per-token overrides layered on top.
tint.condition: the `--tinted` class only when colour tokens actually resolve — a bare `tint-mode` locks the colour scheme without tinting anything

width.description: The track a block rune occupies.

content-measure.description: A page-section rune anchors its content to the text measure when bled to the `wide` track; only the surface and background widen.
content-measure.condition: not author-facing — emitted only when the rune declares `contentMeasure: "anchored"`

density.description: How tightly a rune packs its content (SPEC-025).
density.condition: always present on the rune root; resolution is author ▸ the parent rune's `childDensity` ▸ this rune's `defaultDensity` ▸ `full`

reading.description: Editorial register for body text (SPEC-108). The author picks the register; the theme owns the magnitude.
reading.condition: suppressed at the `ui` default, so unmarked bodies carry no attribute

dropcap.condition: honoured only when the resolved reading register enables it (`prose`); dropped with a warning otherwise

elevation.description: The chrome/depth ladder (SPEC-107). The skin maps each rung to a chrome bundle by attribute, so there is no BEM class.
elevation.condition: emitted only when the author sets it or the rune declares `defaultElevation`

prominence.description: Header emphasis (SPEC-107). Scales a rune's page-section header; the skin maps it to a type register by attribute, so there is no BEM class.
prominence.condition: requires a page-section header — a `sections` role of header, preamble, title or description. Dropped with a warning otherwise.

motion.description: Scroll-reveal entrance (SPEC-105). The author declares the character, the theme owns the choreography, a behaviour owns the timing.
motion.condition: `--rf-reveal-index` is stamped on the cascade items named by the rune's `staggerItems`; without `staggerItems`, `stagger` marks the root and nothing else

content-place.description: The cover overlay anchor (SPEC-089): a 2-axis logical placement (block × inline) that also steers the default scrim so it follows the content edge.
content-place.condition: active only when `media-position` resolves to `cover`; `auto` emits nothing and is left to the CSS container query. `--cover-scrim-dir` here is overridden by an explicit `scrim` edge, which the `cover` axis declares later.

cover.description: Cover-mode chrome (SPEC-089): with `media-position="cover"` the media fills the surface and the content sits over it, so the scrim is rerouted from the background layer to the media well.
cover.target: the rune root, except `data-color-scheme`, which is scoped to the `[data-name="content"]` overlay so only text on the darkened media flips

frame.description: Surface chrome (SPEC-086): a named preset from the theme registry with inline `frame-*` overrides layered on top.
frame.condition: lands on the surface named by `frameTarget`, defaulting to the media zone when the rune declares one. With no target the metas are still consumed but the chrome is dropped with a warning. `data-frame-overflow="bleed"` is stripped with a warning on a clip host.

substrate.description: Generated pattern fills (SPEC-087). Markers only — the engine sets the attributes and cell/opacity custom properties, CSS draws the pattern.
substrate.condition: defaults to the rune root. `substrate-target="media"` moves it to the media zone, and is dropped with a warning on a rune with no media section. The facets are inert without a `substrate` pattern.

bg.description: The background layer (SPEC-088): image, video, gradient, flat overlay wash and legibility scrim, in a single injected layer behind the rune's content.
bg.condition: the layer is raised only when a preset, image, video, gradient, overlay, scrim or `{% bg %}` sandbox guest resolves. In cover mode the scrim is routed to the media well instead, and `data-color-scheme` yields to a scheme a tint already claimed.
